prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity desktop personal website mockup for Aaron Cassar, edge-to-edge at 1440 by 1000 landscape, no browser frame or device. This personal website embraces being almost nothing: incredibly polished, minimal, coder-like, with a secret terminal. Concept: a very small monochrome command-line-shaped introduction centered within enormous warm-neutral white negative space, entirely without a window frame, chrome, box or border. Single text column about 470 pixels wide. First line tiny steel-gray '~/aaron'. Name 'Aaron Cassar' in modest medium IBM Plex Mono-like type. One line 'Software engineer. Maker of things.' A small gap then a row 'work   about   contact'. Further down, a real command prompt 'visitor@aaron ~ %' followed by a solid blue-black rectangular cursor. Tiny hint below 'try “help”, or just say hello.' The prompt is clickable and hints that the website can turn into a fully interactive command terminal. Footer with 'GitHub ↗   LinkedIn ↗   Résumé ↗' at bottom left and a small sun outline theme control at bottom right. Colors only soft off-white, blue-black and muted steel gray. Precise typography, exceptional whitespace, extremely restrained sizes. No green-on-black hacker cliché, gradients, cards, shadows, decorative numbers, big hero statement, photographs or illustrations. It should look intentional and intriguing, like a small live program left open on a very clean sheet of paper.
